Global Industrial Machinery Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Industrial Machinery Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Industrial Machinery Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Global Industrial Machinery Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. First, we delivered strong total revenue growth reflecting robust demand across construction, mining, agriculture, and manufacturing end markets. Second, our operating margins expanded notably by segment, showcasing the effectiveness of our pricing and productivity efforts. Third, inventory levels have been optimized through smart management strategies, improving our working capital efficiency. Fourth, our backlog reached impressive levels with clear conversion timelines into future revenue. Fifth, demand trends in key end markets remain positive, supporting our book-to-bill above 1.2 times. And sixth, we're providing raised operating margin guidance for Q4 and the full year, positioning us for sustained profitability.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. Turning to our financial performance, Global Industrial Machinery Inc. reported $4.3 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This builds on the momentum from prior periods, with organic growth of 11%, acquisitions adding a point and a half, and foreign exchange acting as a slight drag. Let me break this down further. For context, in our Discrete Automation division—including CNC machining centers, robotic welding systems, and precision assembly lines—we generated about $1.72 billion, up 18% year-over-year, driven by demand for next-gen robotic arms with AI path optimization holding solid market share in automotive and semiconductor applications. Our Process Automation segment, covering hydraulic presses and material handling for heavy industry, contributed around $840 million, up 12%, with aftermarket services growing their share thanks to predictive maintenance platforms. Services and Digital Solutions rounded it out at roughly $510 million, up 9%, from cloud-based asset management software connected to thousands of assets globally.

Regionally, North America was the leader at about $2.365 billion, up 22%, fueled by CHIPS Act semiconductor capex and reshoring. EMEA added $900 million, growing 11% amid renewable energy traction, while APAC contributed $645 million, up 8% in constant currency, navigating tariffs through localization. For the full year to date, we're tracking toward strong double-digit growth, outpacing the broader market, with a record backlog providing visibility.

Gross margin expanded to 32.4%, benefiting from favorable mix and cost productivity. Operating expenses were controlled effectively, resulting in consolidated operating income reflecting our disciplined approach. Our net income for the quarter was solid, delivering earnings per share ahead of expectations. Before we go further, let me dive deep into our operating margin performance by segment for Q3. Overall, we delivered a consolidated operating margin of 14.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year and 50 basis points sequentially. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in three years, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward high-margin aftermarket services, aggressive cost-out initiatives, and easing supply chain headwinds.

Starting with Industrial Automation, 28% of total revenue at $1.2 billion, up 12% year-over-year. Operating margins expanded to 18.5%, a 320 basis point improvement from 15.3% last year. Pricing discipline added 150 basis points with 4-6% list price increases on PLCs and SCADA systems, supported by our installed base in automotive and semiconductors. Cost productivity shone through our Smart Factory 2.0 initiative, deploying AI-driven predictive maintenance and digital twins, reducing downtime by 22% and costs by 8%. North America hit 20.1% on reshoring, Europe 16.8% despite energy costs, Asia-Pacific 19.2% on EV builds. We expect mid-18s going forward with IIoT subscriptions at 25% of mix.

Heavy Machinery, our largest at 35% or $1.5 billion, up 8% organically, saw margins at 12.1%, up 90 basis points sequentially as destocking normalized. Aftermarket parts grew 18% to $420 million, lifting margins 200 basis points, though steel inflation capped gains. LeanMach delivered $60 million savings via robotic welding and supplier consolidation. North America 13.4% on IIJA, LatAm softer at 10.5%, APAC 12.8%. Targeting 14% plus with premium engines and telematics.

Aerospace & Defense Components, 22% at $950 million, up 15%, margins at 13.8%, up 250 basis points on Boeing and Airbus ramps. Supply chain normalization unlocked inventory profits, CMMC compliance secured DoD contracts. U.S. 15.2%, Europe 12.5%, MENA 14%. Aiming for 15% plus.

Energy Equipment Systems, 15% at $650 million, up 10%, margins 11.2%, up 180 basis points on LNG and renewables services up 22%. GreenShift platform added premium pricing. North America 12.5%, Europe 9.8%, Middle East/Asia 12%. To 13% with electrolyzers.

In summary, weighted average 13.9%, every segment expanding through pricing, productivity, and services now 32% company-wide. Our $500 million cost actions and digital thread support 15% plus in FY25.

Good morning, everyone. Before we open it up to Q&A, I want to provide some color on our operating margin guidance for Q4 and the full fiscal year 2024. Operating margin remains key, reflecting topline to bottom-line conversion amid input costs and mix shifts. For Q4, guiding 13.0% to 14.0%, up from Q3's 12.5%, sequential 50-150 basis points expansion from pricing, volume leverage, and cost-outs. Full year FY2024 now 13.2% to 13.8%, improved from prior 12.8-13.5%, ahead of FY23's 11.9%, strongest since pre-COVID, upper end vs. peers like Caterpillar at 13-14%.

Positives: Pricing power robust, passed 80% raw material inflation, layering mid-single-digit increases on CNCs, presses, assembly systems. North America 45% revenue, receptive on IIJA/CHIPS, pull-forward for chillers. North America Q4 over 15%, aftermarket up 18% YoY at 28% revenue, 40% plus gross. Europe 25% mix, 11-12% on energy/Ukraine, offset by renewables—wind nacelle orders up 25% QoQ, targeting 10% offshore gearbox share vs. Siemens Gamesa. Asia-Pacific 30%, 14-15%, China sourcing down to 12%, Vietnam/India Pune facility shaves 200 bps logistics.

Technical pillars: Industry 4.0 IoT predictive maintenance on 70% of 150,000 machines, $120M service revenue, 98% uptime, 85% SaaS margins. Lean ERP SAP S/4HANA, RPA in welding/painting, $80M savings, inventory days 85 to 72. Sustainable steel 40% low-carbon with Nucor/ArcelorMittal, hedging CBAM.

Risks: Labor 5-6% inflation, cobots automated 15% assembly but machinist shortages; freight +50 bps on Red Sea; geopolitics/tariffs at low end; energy capex softening. 'Margin-First': 65% in-house fab, services to 35% FY26, $300M German laser M&A. ROIC 18% vs. Deere 16%, PACCAR 15%. Backlog $4.2B up 22% YoY supports outlook.

Now, turning to backlog. Total backlog at quarter-end $4.2 billion, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially. Seventh straight quarter expansion, book-to-bill 1.28x above 1.1-1.2x target. New equipment $2.85 billion (68%), aftermarket/services $945 million (23%), spares $420 million (9%). North America 52% ($2.184B) up 15% on CHIPS/IRA; APAC 28% ($1.176B) up 45% on EV/PLI; EMEA 15% ($630M) on hydrogen; LatAm 5% ($210M) mining.

Conversion: 65% next 12 months, 88% in 24, balance by 2026 end. Improved from 62% prior via $150M Spartanburg capex. Trends: Dual-sourcing cut lead times 20%, AI nesting shaved 15% cycles, cobots faster. North America supercycle, APAC tariffs mitigated Vietnam, Europe ECB cuts. Supports FY24 revenue $4.2-4.4B, 75% from backlog, margins +150-200 bps H2. $200M FY25 capex Monterrey nearshoring, book-to-bill >1.2x. Risks steel +8% YoY, mitigators CPI escalators.

Next, demand trends across construction (42% revenue), mining (28%), agriculture (18%), manufacturing (12%)—85% total. Orders up 12% YoY to $2.8B, book-to-bill 1.25x, backlog $14.5B up 18%.

Construction orders +15% YoY $1.2B, NA IIJA excavators +22%, EMEA +8%, APAC mixed. Electric excavator $150M pilots, pricing +4.2%, aftermarket 68%.

Mining +20% $780M on copper/iron, LatAm +25%, NA +12%, Australia +18%. Command systems +15-20% productivity, backlog 30%.

Ag +5% $500M normalized crops, US +8%, Brazil +12%. See & Spray 77% chem cut, autonomy R&D, services +11%.

Manufacturing +9% $340M, NA EV +16%, APAC +3%. AI palletizers $80M, services 35%.

Regions: NA 55% +14%, EMEA 8%, APAC 10%, LatAm 16%. Dealer inventory 8.5 months. FY24 growth 8-12%, $1.2B capex electrification/autonomy.

Finally, inventory at $452 million, down 13% QoQ from $520M, 18% YoY. Raw $181M down 15%, WIP $113M down 12%, FG $158M down 11%. Added 210 bps gross margin, $22M reserve release. Turns 4.2x up from 3.8x, DIO 87 vs. 96, ahead peers. NA 82 DIO reshoring, Europe 95 energy, APAC 78 pivot India/Vietnam.

SmartStock 2025: SAP/Blue Yonder 92% accuracy, cut buffers 25%; RFID/IoT +18% efficiency, VMI 15% raw; CTO modular WIP 45 to 28 days. Emissions cut 12%. Stabilize $440-460M year-end, turns 4.1-4.3x.

We are managing our capital allocation effectively, prioritizing investments in high-growth areas and returning capital to shareholders.

Next, I will hand over to Michael Torres, COO, for an operational update.

Michael Torres (COO):
Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we've been focused on improving productivity and efficiency across our manufacturing facilities. We've implemented lean manufacturing principles like LeanMach and Smart Factory 2.0, leveraging data analytics and AI for predictive maintenance to reduce downtime and costs. Inventory optimization through SmartStock has been key, alongside supply chain resilience via dual-sourcing and VMI. We're also investing in new technologies to enhance resilience, including modular assembly and cobot automation to address labor challenges.

And I would like to turn the call over to our CTO, Dr. Elena Vasquez, for an update on our technology roadmap.

Dr. Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, Michael. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers. We are investing in research and development in areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. Our new ApexEdge IoT platform is showing promising early results, with over 15,000 connected assets delivering 98% uptime, $120 million in incremental service revenue, and high-margin SaaS streams. Industry 4.0 digital twins, EdgeAI controllers reducing cycle times 25%, GreenShift hydrogen-ready turbines, and autonomy like See & Spray and Command systems are transforming operations. We believe these technologies will transform the industrial landscape and create significant opportunities for Global Industrial Machinery Inc.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from David Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Lee (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question, David. Our digital solutions, anchored by ApexEdge IIoT and TitanGuard predictive maintenance, are accelerating. Subscription revenue is up 15-25% across segments, now 25% of Industrial Automation mix, with 70% rollout on our 150,000-machine base generating $120 million incrementally. AI-driven digital twins cut downtime 22%, boost uptime to 98%, and unlock 85% margin SaaS. In EVs and semis, EdgeAI optimizes paths and nesting, shaving 15-25% cycles. Services now 32% company-wide, targeting 35-20% by FY26, driving book-to-bill 1.4x in automation. Reshoring and ESG tailwinds position us for sustained double-digit growth here.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

Johnathan Hale:
Great question, Maria. Emerging markets, especially APAC and LatAm at 33% of backlog, are priorities. We've reduced China sourcing to 12%, ramping Vietnam/India with Pune facility shaving logistics 200 bps, and Monterrey capex for nearshoring. LatAm mining up 16-25% on BHP/Vale, Brazil assembly dodging tariffs. India's PLI and infrastructure push 25% YoY, with modular robots to Foxconn. Bookings up 45% APAC, targeting 10% share in offshore wind/electrolyzers. $200 million FY25 capex, acquisitions like German laser tuck-in, and CTO models ensure margin-accretive expansion into these high-growth areas.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline (Morgan Stanley):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

Michael Torres:
Thanks, Robert. Skilled labor shortages are industry-wide, with U.S. wage inflation at 5-6%, but we've automated 15% of assembly via Fanuc cobots and RPA, boosting productivity 10-18%. Workforce development includes training tied to Industry 4.0, upskilling for AI/ML and predictive maintenance. Partnerships for machinists, Six Sigma gains, and VMI reduce manual needs. In plants, we've cut scrap 15%, DIO to 87 days. Retention 95% via ESG and digital tools. This sustains 97% on-time delivery while navigating shortages effectively.

Operator:
Seeing no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Industrial Machinery Inc. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
